names.reason: The deciding line is the Q4 profit guide and the September/October credit trend, and neither is visible beforehand. Qualitatively, the inputs since the August call (the collection clean-up, the 30 September marketing rules, bank partner cuts, a former-CRO CEO in his first quarter) point to a guide at or below the freshly cut ~RMB400M Q4 consensus. But the price, at about 1.8x FY27 consensus and below net cash, after a 50% sector-wide fall, plausibly already holds a worse outcome than that. I cannot show which side of that line the release lands on with 65% confidence.
names.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 non-GAAP guide at or above ~RMB400M with management saying C-M2/FPD peaked in August-September and improved in October, or a new 2027 buyback authorisation, would make this a likely sharp up-move. A Q4 guide well under RMB300M or a loss, or a statement that collections keep worsening, would make it a down-move.

A Q4 guide at a loss or withheld, or C-M2 still rising in Oct-Nov, would make the downside right.

The share price fell mostly with the sector, not on AMBA-specific estimate cuts, so a below-seasonal Q4 guide is not shown to be priced. Partly offset: the market also gives almost no value to a reported $95-100 deal.

names.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 revenue guide midpoint at or above about $112M, with management saying memory has not hurt customer orders, would make a relief rally from this washed-out level the likely outcome.
names.unpriced: Possibly the memory effect on the Q4 guide. Consensus for the January quarter ($112.6M) still matches normal seasonality, although management made that conditional on memory and the memory shortage worsened after the call. Revenue estimates were not revised for it, only EPS was trimmed slightly. But the stock's 15% fall today and 23% fall over the month may already price a soft guide, even though most of the month's fall tracks the sector. I cannot show which side of that the price sits on, so the edge is weak.

names.reason: The lean up rests mainly on the ADS's stale discount to HK parity and a probable FX-gain headline. The gap is microstructure, mostly inside the deadband, and depends on the ADS trading before 13:00 ET. The line that decides the reaction, Q3 same-store sales and table turnover, has no public leading data, and HK investors have repeatedly sold this name after prints. Below the 65 threshold, with no informational mechanism, so no trade.
names.what_would_flip_it: Q3 same-store sales negative again, with North America turnover still falling and the operating margin not above Q3-25's 5.9%, would push it down despite the FX-gain headline.
names.unpriced: Only two small things, neither an information edge worth acting on. (1) The ADS's last print ($9.81) is about 2.4% below where it usually sits against HK parity, a microstructure gap that a release-day trade tends to close. (2) The likely Q3 FX swing to a gain will make headline net profit leap YoY, which a headline-driven US reader may not have adjusted for. Neither shows the operating line will beat.

names.reason: The best-evidenced edge is the stale ADS quote against HK parity plus an FX-flattered net profit headline. But the ADS trades a few hundred shares a day and has often not repriced inside the morning window: in Q2 it printed unchanged at 13:00 ET before HK fell 6.9% the next day. With a real chance of no trade, or a stale one, before 13:00, and HK's pre-result session on 25 Nov unknown, the probability is well short of 65.
names.what_would_flip_it: A weak same-store sales line (total SSS down several percent, or North America or Southeast Asia turnover falling) or a cautious call at 07:00 ET, priced by an early ADS trade below 9.8. Or a sharp HK fall in the 25 Nov session, which would erase the parity gap before the release.
names.unpriced: Two small things, neither strong enough to trade. (1) The last ADS print, 9.81, sits about 3% below parity with today's HK close, about 2.4% after the usual -0.9% discount; a thin quote that is behind its underlying. Nobody publishes a usable consensus that shows this is modelled. Whether the thin US market acts on it before 13:00 ET is doubtful.
